rooms.16103: Two walls of wet black rock rise on either hand, so close and so tall that the sky is no more than a pale grey ribbon far overhead. Mist creeps between them like milk poured into a crack, beading every ledge with cold water. The gorge runs on south between the cliffs, while a way down drops over loose scree to the bare, snow-patched slopes of the Northern Wilderness. High on both walls, old white streaks mark the ledges where ravens nest.
rooms.16104: The gorge pinches in here until you could almost touch both walls at once, their faces slick with seepage and furred with black moss. A rough stair of fallen slabs climbs up out of the cleft to a mountain path, each step worn hollow by feet older than memory. Northward the gorge winds back toward its mouth above the wilderness. Every footfall comes back as a hollow, doubled echo, and the air tastes of wet iron.
rooms.16105: The stair from the gorge ends on a shelf of broken slate where the wind finds you at last, cold and wet off the mist. Two ways part here: a path running south along the mountain's shoulder toward a summit hidden in cloud, and a narrower track creeping west along a ledge. Behind you the rough stair drops down into the gorge between the mountain walls. Tufts of coarse grass shiver in every crack, strung with droplets like beads.
rooms.16106: The path steepens into a scramble over tilted slabs of black rock streaked with rusty orange lichen. From here a last steep pitch leads up to the mountain top, which rounds away into the cloud above. North, the path runs back along the shoulder to the shelf where the ways part. The wind has found a voice among the slabs, keening through every crack, and old snow clings in the shadow of each boulder.
rooms.16107: You stand on the mountain top, a bald crown of black rock scoured smooth by the wind and glistening with the endless mist. On a squat stone plinth sits an iron beacon basket, rusted red and long cold, left from the days when warning fires were lit here. Mostly the cloud presses close, but when it tears open the world falls away beneath you in a sudden, dizzying sweep of grey peaks and dark forest. The only way off is back down the steep pitch.
rooms.16108: A narrow ledge runs along the face of the mountain, scarcely wider than a handcart, with a drop beside it that vanishes into grey nothing. Iron pegs hammered into the rock make a crude ladder going up to a higher shelf, their heads polished bright by generations of gripping hands. East, the ledge leads back to where the ways part above the gorge. Water drips steadily from an overhang into a shallow basin worn in the stone.
rooms.16110: The pegged climb tops out on a broad shelf where several ways meet among tumbled boulders. Ledges run off east and west along the cliff, a steep cleft leads up toward higher ground, and the iron pegs go back down to the ledge below. In the middle of the shelf someone has stacked a small cairn of flat stones. A scrap of grey cloth, bleached by sun and rain, flutters from a stick wedged in its top.
rooms.16109: The ledge stops dead at the lip of a sheer drop, where the rock simply ends and the mist begins. Gusts boil up from below, smelling of wet stone and, very faintly, of pine. When the cloud is torn aside you can see straight down a thousand feet of black cliff to fans of scree and the tops of trees, a sight that turns the knees to water. West is the only way, back to the boulder-strewn shelf.
rooms.16111: A short spur of path ends beneath a deep overhang, a natural shelter where the wind cannot quite reach. A ring of fire-blackened stones and a smear of old charcoal show that others have waited out storms here. The underside of the overhang is crusted with abandoned nests of sticks and wool, glued fast with droppings. East, the path leads back to the shelf where the ways meet.
rooms.16112: The cleft from the shelf below opens onto a high, windswept path where loose stones skitter at every step. Mist drags across the slope in long grey veils, hiding the next few yards one moment and the next drawing back to bare the black teeth of the crags all around. The path runs on west across the slope, and the cleft leads back down to the meeting of the ways. Juniper crouches flat against the rock, its berries frosted blue.
rooms.16113: Here the path crosses a long slope of shattered grey slate whose fragments clink and slide underfoot like broken crockery. Above and below, the scree runs off into the mist, and the whole slope seems ready to shift at one careless step. Someone has laid flat stones edge to edge to make a rough causeway across the worst of it, running east and west. The air is thin and bitter, and it rasps in the chest.
rooms.16114: The causeway of laid stones ends at a sharp corner, where the path turns south around a rough buttress of rock. Rain has carved deep runnels down the buttress, and a thin waterfall spills from one of them into a pool before slipping away across the path. Eastward the causeway runs back over the scree. Thick cushions of moss, startlingly green against the dark rock, grow wherever the spray can reach.
rooms.16115: Three ways meet on a saddle of wet turf between two rocky knolls. North, the path bends back around the buttress toward the scree; east, a faint track leads out onto a narrow spur; west, the main path carries on along the mountain's flank. Mist pools in the saddle like water in a bowl, and the turf squelches underfoot. A weathered post still stands crookedly at the junction, though the sign it once carried has long since rotted away.
rooms.16116: The faint track runs out along a narrow spur of rock and stops at its blunt end, where a single wind-bent pine clings on with roots like clutching fingers. The tree leans so far over the edge that its crown hangs above nothing at all. Far below, mist fills the valley from wall to wall like a sea of grey wool. The only way is back west to the saddle.
rooms.16117: The path meets the foot of a steep gully here, choked with boulders, that leads up the mountainside toward higher ledges. A short ledge strikes off west, while the path runs back east to the misty saddle. Meltwater trickles down the gully between the stones, and every boulder is slick with green slime. High above, the walls of the gully vanish into the cloud.
rooms.16118: This short ledge ends against a sheer slab of rock, polished by running water into a dark mirror that gives back a dim, warped reflection. Long scratches mark the slab at about the height of a man's chest, as though something heavy has clawed at it and failed to climb. A cold draught breathes from a crack at its foot. There is nothing for it but to return east to the bottom of the gully.
rooms.16119: The boulder gully tops out on a narrow path cut into the mountainside, walled by dripping rock on one hand and open to a sudden drop on the other. Where the way is steepest, square steps have been chiselled into the stone, very old and rounded by weather. The path runs on west, and the gully leads down among its slimy boulders. Rime clings to every crack in the wall, glittering faintly in the grey light.
rooms.16120: The path runs level along a ledge beneath a long overhang, so that a lid of black rock hangs just above your head while open air yawns at your other side. Icicles fringe the lip of the overhang, dripping onto the path and freezing again into knobbly lumps underfoot. The ledge continues east and west. Below, the mist lies so thick that the drop looks almost solid enough to walk on.
rooms.16121: The ledge widens into a rough terrace where a steep path branches down the mountainside, zigzagging toward forested slopes far below. The main path carries on west toward a line of higher crags and runs back east beneath the overhang. Heather grows thick on the terrace, brown and wiry and beaded with mist. On clearer days thin threads of smoke can be seen rising from among the distant trees.
rooms.16122: The path passes beneath a crag where a rough chimney in the rock leads up to a higher ledge, its sides worn smooth by climbing hands and knees. West, the path runs on toward a dark barrier just visible through the mist; east, it returns to the heather terrace. Old iron rings, rusted brown, are set into the rock beside the chimney, perhaps once for ropes. The wind moans in the chimney like breath across the mouth of a jug.
rooms.16123: The path is closed here by a stout gate of lashed pine trunks, built across a gap between two boulders and barred with a beam as thick as a man's thigh. Through the mist beyond it a wider path runs west toward the steep, dark roof of a large cabin, but the gate is chained and frozen fast. Strange signs have been daubed on the gateposts in some dark, rusty stain. The only open way is back east along the mountain path.
rooms.16128: The chimney opens at its top onto a high, airy ledge running along the face of the mountain. West, the ledge leads into thickening mist, and east it ends in a nook in the cliff. At your feet the chimney drops back down to the path below, a dark slot in the rock. The wind here is fierce and steady, flattening the few plants that grow and singing over the edge.
rooms.16127: The ledge ends in a shallow nook, scooped out of the cliff by frost and sheltered from the worst of the wind. Its floor is matted with sticks, moulted black feathers and the white splashes of years of droppings, the leavings of the great birds that roost here. A sour smell of carrion hangs in the still air. West, the ledge runs back to the head of the chimney.
rooms.16129: The path crosses a broad face of slabby black rock tilted at a steep angle, where every step must be placed with care on the wet stone. Shallow grooves cut across the slabs give a little grip, and a rusted chain stapled to the rock serves as a handrail along the worst stretch. The way runs east and west across the face. Water sheets down the rock in a thin, shining film.
rooms.16130: A crack splits the cliff here, and a rough way leads up through it toward higher paths, its floor a staircase of wedged boulders. The main path runs on west along the mountainside and back east across the slabs. Tough grey lichen covers every surface the water does not sweep. When the mist thins, tier after tier of dark crags can be seen rising above you, lost at last in cloud.
rooms.16131: Here the path winds through a field of huge fallen boulders, some as large as cottages, tumbled from the heights in some long-ago landslide. The way threads between them east and west, twisting so that you rarely see more than a few paces ahead. Moss and small ferns grow in the damp shadows at their feet. Deep gouges score one great block, as though something with claws has sharpened them on it.
rooms.16132: The boulders give way to an open stretch of path along the rim of a broad, grassy shelf. Mist rolls across the shelf in waves, and at times you walk in a world of grey with nothing but the path at your feet. Small mossy cairns, knee-high, mark its outer edge every few yards so that walkers do not stray over the drop. The way continues east among the boulders and west along the rim.
rooms.16133: The path narrows between a rock wall and a precipice, and a low parapet of piled stones has been built along the outer edge, though stretches of it have tumbled into the void. A spring wells from a crack in the wall, filling a carved stone trough with icy, clear water, its lip worn smooth by countless hands. The way runs east toward the grassy shelf and west to a wide crossing of paths. Mist curls slowly up over the parapet.
rooms.16134: This is a broad crossing of paths on a high saddle of the mountain, its ground trodden bare and muddy. North, a path climbs onto the rim of the Crescent Cliffs, whose great curve shows dimly through the mist; east and west, long paths follow the mountainside; south, another heads off along a grassy ledge. A tall standing stone, carved with weathered signs, keeps watch at the centre of the crossing. Here the wind seems to blow from every side at once.
rooms.16159: You stand at the first horn of the Crescent Cliffs, where the rim of a vast, curving precipice begins. The edge sweeps away west in a great arc, and on its inner side the rock falls sheer into a bowl of mist so deep that no bottom can be seen. South, a path leads back to the crossing on the saddle. Nests of sticks cling to the ledges just under the rim, and the wind never rests.
rooms.16160: The path keeps close to the rim of the cliffs here, at times no more than an arm's length from the edge. Across the misty gulf, the far arm of the crescent shows as a dark line of crags whenever the cloud thins. The way runs east toward the horn of the cliffs and west along the curving rim. Frost has split the rock underfoot into great blocks, and some of them lean outward as if waiting to fall.
rooms.16161: A stream crosses the clifftop here and pours straight over the edge, falling in a long white plume into the gulf. Its roar fills the air, and a fine cold spray drifts back over the rim, glazing the nearby rocks with ice. Flat stepping stones carry the path over the stream, east and west along the rim. Ferns and mosses grow lush and green in the constant wet, the only soft things on the whole clifftop.
rooms.16162: Here the rim of the cliffs bends sharply, and the path turns with it to run north along the edge of the gulf. East, the rim runs back toward the roar of the waterfall. A pillar of rock, split away from the cliff by frost, stands just off the edge across a gap that no sane traveller would try to leap. Its flat top is heaped with old nests and whitened with droppings.
rooms.16163: A side path leaves the rim here, heading west away from the edge across the open mountainside. The clifftop runs on north and south, curving gently, with the gulf a vast grey hollow at your feet. A low stone hut, roofless and half collapsed, crouches beside the path, perhaps once a lookout's shelter. Thin grass and starry white saxifrage grow between its fallen stones.
rooms.16164: The rim narrows to a knife-edge of rock, with the gulf on one side and a steep run of scree on the other. A rope of twisted hide, stiff with age, has been strung between iron stakes along the crest as a handline, and the path follows it north and south. When the wind gusts it is hard to stay upright. Through rents in the mist you may glimpse the black water of a tarn far, far below.
rooms.16165: This is the far bend of the crescent, where the rim turns once more and runs east along the other side of the gulf. A path leaves the cliffs to the west, heading toward the tall wall of a tower that shows dimly through the mist. South, the knife-edge crest runs back along the rim. A great cairn, taller than a man, has been raised here at the turning, and every passing hand seems to have added a stone.
rooms.16167: Along this stretch the clifftop is broad and grassy, but the rim has crumbled into a row of jagged bays, and the path keeps well back from them. It runs east along the crescent and west toward the great cairn at the bend. Clumps of pink thrift and wiry grass grow among the rocks, pressed flat by the gusts. A wet wind blows across the gulf, carrying a fine, drifting rain.
rooms.16168: Here the cliff juts out in a great overhang, and the path runs along its very top, so that the rock beneath your feet hangs over empty air. Through cracks in the overhang you can see the mist swirling straight below. The path continues east and west along the rim. Frost-shattered rock lies everywhere, and it is plain that pieces of this ledge break away into the gulf each winter.
rooms.16169: The clifftop rises into a hump of bare black rock, and from its crown, when the mist allows, the whole sweep of the crescent can be seen curving away behind you. The rim narrows ahead to the east and runs back west across the hump. Deep scratches score the rock in sets of three, too broad and too deep for any bird, where something heavy lands often. The drop into the gulf is sheer and dizzying.
rooms.16170: The rim of the cliffs ends here at the far horn of the crescent, a narrow point of rock thrust out over the gulf. There is nothing beyond but cloud and the endless sound of the wind. An iron spike has been driven deep into the rock at the very tip, with a few rotted strands of rope still knotted around it. From this lonely point the clifftop runs back west along the crescent.
rooms.16166: The path heads west from the cliffs toward a tall, round tower of dark stone that looms larger with every step, its top lost in the cloud. The ground is a rough slope of heather and broken rock, cut by little runnels of water. East, the way leads back to the great cairn on the rim of the Crescent Cliffs. Hobnailed boots have left their marks in the muddy patches, some going toward the tower and some coming away.
rooms.16187: You stand at the foot of a tall, round tower whose curving wall of dark, rough-dressed stone rises sheer into the mist above you. A path circles the base of the tower, running north and west around the curve, while the way east leads back toward the Crescent Cliffs. No door shows in the wall on this side, only narrow slits far overhead. The lowest courses of stone are green with moss and pitted by weather.
rooms.16188: The path curves around the foot of the tower, the dark wall always at your shoulder. A doorway was once set into the stone here, but it has been blocked up with rough blocks and lumpy mortar, now cracked and sprouting weeds. The path continues north and south around the curve. Water drips steadily from the masonry, and the ground at the wall's foot is a strip of puddles and moss.
rooms.16189: Beside the tower, a narrow crevice opens in the mountainside to the east, but it is choked with fallen boulders and a tangle of frozen thornbrush, and no one has forced a way through in years. The path around the tower runs south and west along the curve of the wall. Crude arrows and runes have been scratched into the tower stones at shoulder height. The mist hangs heavy and still in the lee of the wall.
rooms.16190: On this side of the tower the ground falls away sharply, and a short path leads north onto a jutting spur of rock where, it is said, the finest view on the mountain is to be had. The path around the tower runs east and west along its curving wall. Arrow slits high in the masonry stare out over the spur. The wind blows hard and cold here, tugging at your clothes.
rooms.16171: You stand at the tip of a rocky spur thrust out from the mountain, and when the mist parts the whole realm seems to open beneath you. Dark forests roll away below, a glacier glitters beyond them among white snowfields, and far off the land fades into a blue haze where rivers wind and the smoke of distant towns rises. The drop from the spur is sheer on three sides, enough to turn the strongest stomach. The only way back is south to the foot of the tower.
rooms.16191: Here the tower wall is scorched black in a broad smear, as though a great fire once raged against it, and the stones are cracked and flaking from the heat. The path curves around the base, east toward the spur of the great view and south along the wall. Charred stumps of timber jut from sockets in the masonry, all that remains of some wooden stair or gallery. Sooty water drips from them onto the path.
rooms.16192: The path runs close beneath the tower, which leans very slightly outward here, so that it always seems about to topple onto you. A heap of fallen masonry from the upper wall lies half buried in moss beside the path. The way leads north and south around the base. Ferns sprout from the cracks, and a thin stream of water trickles from a slit far above, spattering onto the stones.
rooms.16185: The path bends around the curve of the tower, its foot a jumble of mossy rocks and old grey snow that never quite melts in the shadow of the wall. A wooden stake has been driven into the ground at the bend, hung with small skulls and strings of black feathers, a warning or a ward. The way continues north and east around the base. Above, the top of the tower is lost in the cloud.
rooms.16186: The path around the tower meets a track here, which leads south away from the wall across a slope of broken rock. East and west, the path follows the tower's curve. A low wall of piled stones forms a rough pen against the tower's base, once perhaps for goats, now empty and full of nettles. Mist trails across the face of the tower like smoke from a doused fire.
rooms.16177: Three ways meet on a slope of broken rock below the tower, whose dark bulk stands to the north at the end of a short track. East, a path winds off toward the Crescent Cliffs; west, another runs along the mountainside into the mist. The rocks here are spattered with orange and yellow lichen, the brightest colours on the whole grey mountain. A thin, cold rain falls more often than not.
rooms.16176: The path turns a corner around a jutting crag, heading south along the mountainside and west toward the paths below the tower. A small shrine has been built into a niche in the crag, a shelf of flat stone bearing a carved figure so worn that it is impossible to tell whether it is a man or a bird. Pebbles and scraps of bright cloth have been left on the shelf as offerings. The mist drips from everything.
rooms.16173: Ways part on a shelf of rock beneath a dripping cliff. North, the path bends around a crag; east, it leads toward the Crescent Cliffs; south, it continues across a slope of tumbled rocks. A deep pool lies in a hollow of the shelf, black and cold and fed by the drips from above. Thick moss rims its edge like a collar of green velvet.
rooms.16172: The path runs along the foot of a low ridge, joining the Crescent Cliffs to the east with the ways that wander west across the mountain. The ridge shelters the path from the worst of the wind, and heather grows thick and springy underfoot. Scattered boulders wear caps of green moss. Now and again the mist pulls back to show the rim of the cliffs, sharp against a grey sky.
rooms.16174: The path picks its way across a slope of tumbled black rocks, each one slick with wet and blotched with white lichen. It runs north toward the pool beneath the dripping cliff and west toward the edge of a ravine. The gaps between the rocks are deep enough to swallow a leg, and the footing is treacherous. A thin sleet comes on the wind, stinging the face.
rooms.16175: The path bends at the edge of a deep ravine, turning south along its rim and running east back across the tumbled rocks. A stream rushes along the ravine floor far below, white with foam, and its noise rises through the mist. A single flat slab bridges a narrow side cleft. Stunted rowans grow out of the ravine's walls, their red berries bright against the black rock.
rooms.16140: Three paths meet at the head of the ravine, where a stream spills over a lip of rock and plunges out of sight. North, the way follows the ravine's rim; east, a long path runs beneath a cliff; west, a track heads out across a bare slope of scree. The air is loud with rushing water and cold with spray. A crude footbridge of logs, green with moss, crosses the stream.
rooms.16139: The path runs along a sheltered ledge at the foot of a long cliff, whose face is pocked with small caves and hollows. East, the ledge rises toward a grassy shoulder of the mountain; west, it reaches the head of the ravine. Rivulets run down the cliff after every rain, and the ledge is muddy and dotted with puddles. In one of them, preserved in the mud, is the print of an enormous bare foot, broad and long-toed.
rooms.16138: Here the path climbs over a low shoulder of the mountain, a hump of short, wind-bitten grass and scattered stones. From its crest, when the mist lifts, you can follow the path with your eye as it runs away east and west along the flank of the mountain. A single standing stone, waist-high and leaning, marks the crest. The turf is pitted with the small, sharp hoofprints of goats.
rooms.16137: A side path branches south here from the long mountain path, heading toward lower ledges, while the main way runs east and west across the mountainside. A broken signpost leans at the fork, its arms long gone, but a dwarven rune carved into the post still points the way south. Rock and heather stretch away on every side, half hidden in drifting cloud. A small cairn of white quartz stones sits at the foot of the post.
rooms.16136: The path runs along a terrace of flat slate slabs, laid down by nature as neatly as any paving. Water pools in the cracks between them and freezes into a skin of ice that crackles underfoot. The terrace continues east toward a crossing of paths and west toward a broken signpost. Just below the path, mist fills a hollow to the brim, smooth as a pond, and the tops of a few stunted pines poke up through it.
rooms.16135: The path rises gently east toward the crossing of ways on the high saddle and runs back west along the slate terrace. Tall heaps of broken stone, the spoil of some old quarrying, line one side of the path, and the wedge marks of long-dead quarrymen still show in the rock face behind them. The wind flings grit into your eyes. Here and there a stubborn harebell nods in a sheltered crack.
rooms.16145: The side path comes out onto a broad ledge where the ways part again. North lies the fork with the broken signpost; east, a short track runs out to a point of rock; south, the path follows the ledge toward the lower slopes. Rocks fallen from the cliff above litter the ledge, and a few have burst apart on the path. Rough steps cut into the stone show that this was once a well-kept way.
rooms.16146: A short track ends at a point of rock jutting out over the mountainside, its surface scarred by long, deep gouges where great claws have gripped it again and again. Dark streaks stain the stone, and a rank, reptile smell hangs in the air. Below, the mist hides everything but the faint sound of falling water. The only way back is west to the ledge, and it is a relief to take it.
rooms.16152: The ledge curves around a buttress, and the path follows it west toward the turning where it begins its descent to the dwarven lands. North, the ledge runs back toward the parting of the ways. The buttress is banded grey and white, and someone has chiselled neat steps across a gap where the ledge has fallen away. The mist below glows faintly, as if sunlight lies on the valleys beneath it.
rooms.16151: Here the mountain path makes its last turn before it drops toward the village of the dwarves, the turning point that every traveller on the road below looks up to. A broad stair of dressed stone leads down from the ledge, well made in the dwarven way, with grooves cut for grip. East, the ledge runs back around the banded buttress. The air is a little milder here, and the grass grows longer between the stones.
rooms.16141: The track crosses a long, bare slope of grey scree and tilted slabs, heading west toward the foot of a steep crag and east back to the meeting of paths by the stream. Nothing grows here but lichen, and the stones rattle and slide at every step. In the mist the slope seems to go on forever, without top or bottom. A cold wind hisses over the scree like breath through teeth.
rooms.16142: The scree ends against the foot of a steep crag, where a way leads up through a cleft in the rock, scrambling over boulders. East, the track runs back across the scree slope. The cleft is dark and wet, and a cold wind pours down it. Someone has wedged a few logs crosswise in the cleft to serve as steps, and they are worn smooth and slippery.
rooms.16143: The cleft tops out on a steep slope of boulders and rough grass. Above, the slope climbs up toward broken ground at the foot of a sheer peak, and a level track leads west to the same place along the edge of the slope. Down through the cleft lies the long scree slope. Tiny mountain flowers cling to the cracks, white and yellow, and the wind carries the smell of snow.
rooms.16144: This is a rough hollow of hummocky ground and boulders at the base of a sheer peak whose black face rises straight into the cloud. A track leads east toward the head of the cleft, and a steep path goes down a gully toward a ledge below. Tough grass and white tufts of cotton-grass grow in boggy patches, and pools of black water mirror the grey sky. The peak drips constantly, its streams pattering on the rocks.
rooms.16153: A steep gully climbs up from here to a boggy hollow at the base of a sheer peak. West, the path runs along a narrow ledge toward a buttress banded grey and white. Loose stones fill the gully, and every step sends a few clattering away. Sedge and moss grow along the sides of the gully, and the air is damp and still.
rooms.16178: The path runs west from the junction below the tower across a long slope dotted with boulders and tufts of tough grass, heading toward a frozen stream. Eastward it returns to that junction beneath the tower. Mist settles here in heavy banks, and sounds carry strangely through it, so that near noises seem far and far ones near. Patches of old snow lie in the hollows.
rooms.16179: Here the path crosses a frozen stream on a natural bridge of rock, beneath which water gurgles unseen. The way runs east across the boulder-dotted slope and west toward a fork on a saddle. Icicles hang from the underside of the rock bridge, and frost has furred the stones white. The cold here is sharp and still, and the air smells of iron.
rooms.16180: Paths part on a narrow saddle between two hummocks of bare rock. East, the way leads back over the frozen stream; south, a path heads toward the long descent to the mountain's base; west, a short track leads out onto a promontory. A ring of stones marks an old campsite, its ashes long cold and soaked by rain. Mist drifts across the saddle in thick, slow banks.
rooms.16182: The path begins its long descent here, dropping over the edge of the saddle in a series of steep, rocky steps. North, the way returns to the saddle and its old campsite. Below, the mountainside falls away into thinning mist, through which the dark green of forest can sometimes be seen. Loose stones and gravel make the footing slippery.
rooms.16183: The path winds down the steep lower slopes of the mountain in tight turns, the bare rock giving way to grass and patches of heather. Up the slope it climbs back toward the saddle; down below, it reaches the foot of the mountain, where the forest begins. The air grows less bitter as you descend, and the mist thins to a light haze. The first stunted pines grow here, leaning away from the wind.
rooms.16184: You stand at the foot of Mount Ravenmist, where the steep slopes give way to rolling ground of moss and stones. North, the dark trees of the taiga begin, a forest of spruce and pine reaching away into the Northern Wilderness. Behind you, the path climbs up the mountainside in tight switchbacks into the mist. The ground is soft and springy, and the air smells of resin and wet earth.
rooms.16181: The track ends on a promontory of bare rock, ringed by sheer drops. When the mist parts you can look out across a sea of dark forest far below, stretching away until it fades into grey. The rock is scoured clean by the wind, and nothing grows here, not even lichen. A bare spine of rock leads back east to the saddle.
rooms.16147: A grassy ledge runs from the high crossing of paths, north back to the saddle and east along the mountainside. A steep, slippery way also goes down from the ledge, following a long gully. The grass is cropped short by grazing goats, and their droppings dot the turf. The mist rolls up the gully from below, cold and wet, and breaks over the ledge like a slow grey tide.
rooms.16148: The ledge narrows as it runs east along the mountainside toward the scar of a rockfall, with the rock wall leaning close on one side. West, it widens toward the head of the gully. Streaks of rust-red stain the wall where iron-bearing water seeps from the rock. Water drips steadily from above, and every sound comes back from the wall twice over.
rooms.16149: The path crosses the top of a steep slope of loose stones here, the remains of a great rockfall. A rough way has been cleared through the debris, running east and west. Above, a raw pale scar on the cliff shows where the rocks broke away. Some of the boulders have been crushed to fragments, as if by a giant's hammer.
rooms.16150: The ledge ends at the foot of a steep rock step, where a way leads up toward a dark opening high in the cliff. West, the ledge runs back across the rockfall. A faint, sour smell of smoke and sulphur drifts down from above. The rock here is warm to the touch in places, strangely so on this cold mountain.
rooms.16155: The rock step tops out on a narrow ledge before the mouth of a dark cave, which opens just east of you. Down below, the ledge and the rockfall are visible through the mist. The ledge is strewn with black soot and gravel, and the rock around the cave mouth is smudged dark as if by old fires. The air is noticeably warmer here, and it shimmers faintly over the cave.
rooms.16156: You stand just within the mouth of a dark cave, its rough ceiling of black rock low overhead and its walls stained with soot. Grey light comes in from the ledge to the west, but it fails quickly, and the cave runs east into deep darkness. A warm draught blows steadily outward, smelling of smoke and hot stone. The floor is gritty with ash.
rooms.16157: The cave opens into a rough chamber where the darkness is almost total, and the air is warm and close. In the middle of the floor a round shaft goes down into the rock, but it has been sealed with a great slab of stone, cracked across, through which a faint red glow and a breath of heat seep. West, the passage leads back to the cave mouth. The walls are glazed and blistered, as if great heat had once licked them.
rooms.16154: The steep gully runs down the mountainside between walls of crumbling rock, its floor a jumble of loose stones. Up the gully lies the grassy ledge below the crossing of paths; down it, the way reaches the foot of the mountain. The mist is thick and wet, and the walls drip. Rowan and birch saplings cling to the sides of the gully, their roots bared by rain.
rooms.16158: The gully spills out here at the base of the mountain onto a fan of stones and gravel, beyond which the ground is a tangle of boulders, bracken and thorn that no path crosses. The only way on is back up the gully. The walls of a small stone hut stand at the edge of the fan, roofless and filled with nettles. Mist hangs low over everything.
rooms.16124: The path zigzags steeply down the mountainside in tight switchbacks, each turn propped up by a crude wall of piled stones. Up the slope the switchbacks climb back to the heather terrace, and down below the path reaches the foot of the mountain, where dark trees crowd close. Here and there a stake has been driven in beside the path, notched with tally marks in a careful hand. Fresh scrapes on the stones show the path is often used.
rooms.16125: Here the roots of the mountain meet rolling ground of tussock grass and lichen-crusted boulders. Behind you the switchback path climbs up the steep slope into the mist. North, the land runs down to the edge of a forest, where tall dark trees stand shoulder to shoulder like a wall. Muddy boot prints cross the soft ground between the stones, and a thin trail of woodsmoke drifts out from somewhere among the trees.
rooms.16126: You stand beneath the first great trees of the forest, where their boughs knit together overhead into a roof so thick and close that it shuts out the day. The light is dim and green, and the air is still and smells of moss, rot and resin. A small path leads north between mossy trunks into the deep, dark forest beyond. South, a bright gap between the trunks opens onto the open ground at the foot of the mountain.
rooms.12401: The crack runs on through the heart of the glacier, a slot of blue ice barely wide enough for one traveller, its walls leaning together overhead into a roof of cloudy ice. Light seeps through the ice in a deep, strange blue, and every breath hangs before your face. North, a brighter whiteness marks the glacier's end; south, the crack winds back toward the mountains of the Northern Wilderness. The ice creaks and ticks softly around you, as though the glacier were dreaming in its sleep.
rooms.12403: Here the glacier ends in a great wall of dirty blue ice, streaked with grit and studded with boulders, and a narrow crack splits it to the south. Before the ice lies a waste of moraine, heaps of gravel and stones dropped by the glacier and frozen together under a crust of snow. North, beyond the moraine, the first dark pines of the Winterwood rise in a silent wall. The cold here is deep and still, and the air smells of snow.
rooms.12404: The path enters the Winterwood among young pines that have crept out onto the moraine, their boughs bowed low under loads of snow. South, the trees thin toward the glacier's end; west, the path leads deeper into the forest. The snow is wind-packed and firm, and the passing of travellers shows only as a line of shallow dents. A cold breath comes off the ice, stirring the needles with a dry whisper.
rooms.12405: The path bends around a great boulder left behind by the glacier long ago, now wearing a thick cap of snow and a beard of icicles. Eastward the path returns to the edge of the forest; north, it winds on among taller pines. The trees crowd closer here, and the light grows dim, filtered through layer upon layer of snowy boughs. Your footsteps are muffled almost to silence.
rooms.12406: Tall black pines rise on every side, their trunks bare of branches for many feet before they spread into dark crowns heavy with snow. The path runs south past the great capped boulder and west deeper into the trees. Between the trunks the snow lies smooth and unbroken, blue in the shadows. Now and then a clump of snow slips from a high branch and lands with a soft thump.
rooms.12407: The path runs straight here between two ranks of pines, like the aisle of some vast and frozen hall. Old blazes hacked into the bark at head height mark the way east and west, the wounds long since healed into scars crusted with amber resin. The air smells sharply of pitch and cold. High above, the wind combs the crowns of the pines with a sound like distant surf.
rooms.12408: A frozen stream crosses the path, its surface a sheet of grey ice beneath which water can be heard chuckling faintly. Logs have been laid side by side across it to make a crude bridge, now glazed with ice and treacherous underfoot. The path runs on east and west from the stream. Hoarfrost feathers every dead stem along the banks, and the pines lean close over the water.
rooms.12409: The path turns at the foot of a lightning-struck pine, split from crown to root and charred black, yet somehow still standing. East lies the frozen stream and its bridge of logs; south, the path continues among the trees. Snow has drifted into the split trunk, filling it like mortar between stones. The neighbouring pines seem to keep their distance from the ruined tree, as if it were cursed.
rooms.12410: The path dips into a hollow where the snow lies deep and soft, and each step sinks to the knee. North lies the lightning-split pine; west, the path struggles out of the hollow and on through the forest. A ring of young firs stands buried to the shoulders in drifts, only their dark tips showing. A line of wolf tracks crosses the hollow, each print set neatly in the one before.
rooms.12411: The path runs along a low ridge where the wind has scoured the snow thin, and the brown needles of the forest floor show through in patches. East, it drops into the hollow of deep snow; west, it keeps to the crest. The pines on the ridge have been wrung by the wind into strange, crooked shapes. Between their trunks the white land falls away into a blue dimness.
rooms.12412: The path swings around the roots of a giant pine torn up by some winter storm, its upended root plate standing taller than a man and hung with icicles and frozen clods. North, the way continues alongside the fallen trunk; east, it runs back along the ridge. The pit left by the roots has filled with drifted snow. The crown of the tree lies somewhere far off among the others, lost from sight.
rooms.12413: The path runs beside the long fallen trunk, where the snow has drifted against it in a smooth, curling bank. South, the way bends around the great root plate; west, it reaches a clearing where paths meet. Small tracks cross and recross the snow here, the neat prints of hares and the straight-stepping line of a fox. Your breath hangs in the still air and drifts slowly away.
rooms.12414: Three paths meet in a small clearing among the pines, where the snow lies trampled and grey. North, a path leads toward rising, rocky ground; east, the way runs beside a fallen trunk; west, a fainter track wanders off among the trees toward a scatter of boulders. In the middle of the clearing stands a waymark post, carved with the figure of a stag and capped with snow. The surrounding pines are tall and utterly still.
rooms.12415: The path climbs gently northward as the ground begins to rise toward a ridge of rock. South, it returns to the clearing with the waymark post. Pines grow here from cracks in the boulders, their roots clutching the stone like the fingers of old men. Snow lies heaped on every rock and branch, and icicles hang in fringes from the outcrops.
rooms.12416: The rising ground grows steeper, and the path picks its way north between boulders and the knuckled roots of pines. South, the way slopes back toward the clearing. A frozen spring has spilled a fan of white ice down the face of one great boulder, rippled like a curtain caught in a draught. The trees creak and groan in the wind, a sound like ships at anchor.
rooms.12417: The path reaches the foot of a rocky ridge, where a narrow way leads up into a dark cleft in the rock. East, the main path runs on along the foot of the ridge; south, it returns among the boulders. The mouth of the cleft is half choked with drifted snow, and a cold draught sighs out of it. Pines lean out over it from the ridge, their roots clinging to bare stone.
rooms.12418: The path follows the foot of the ridge before turning north into deep forest. West, it returns to the snowy mouth of the cleft. Icicles as long as spears hang from an overhang of the ridge, and the snow beneath them is pocked with holes where their drips have fallen. Northward the trees stand dark and dense, a wall of black trunks.
rooms.12419: The path runs through a stand of ancient pines, their trunks so thick that three men could not link arms around them. Their bark is deeply furrowed and stained with old resin, and their boughs meet high overhead in a dark, unbroken canopy. Little snow reaches the ground beneath them, and the path is a carpet of brown needles. The way leads north and south between the giants.
rooms.12420: The ancient pines give way to younger trees, and the snow returns, lying deep and powdery on the path. North, the way leads to a meeting of paths; south, it enters the stand of great old pines. Through gaps in the branches the sky shows hard and pale as a sheet of tin. A cold wind sighs through the treetops, and loose snow sifts down in glittering veils.
rooms.12421: Three ways meet here in the deep forest beside a great boulder glazed with ice. East, a narrow path slips between close-set firs; south, the way returns through the young pines; west, the main path runs on into the trees. Above the junction the crowns of the pines part to leave a ragged window on the sky. By night the stars burn cold and close through it, and the snow gleams faintly in their light.
rooms.12452: The narrow path winds between close-set firs whose snowy branches brush your shoulders and shower you with powder. North, it goes on deeper into the wood; west, it returns to the junction by the icy boulder. Few feet come this way, and the snow on the path lies smooth. A small spring trickles from beneath a rock, edged with ice that never quite closes over it.
rooms.12453: The path climbs gently through a stand of birches, their white bark peeling in papery curls and their bare twigs a purple haze against the snow. North, the way continues among them; south, it returns among the firs. The birches stand ghostly pale against the dark pines beyond. Snow lies in the forks of their branches like tufts of raw wool.
rooms.12454: The ground grows rocky here and the trees thin, so that a tall cliff of grey stone can be seen rising beyond them, gleaming with ice. The path turns east toward the foot of the cliff and runs back south among the birches. Boulders fallen from the cliff lie half buried in snow. In the stillness you can hear a faint trickle of water hidden somewhere beneath the ice.
rooms.12455: The path ends at the foot of a sheer cliff, down which a waterfall has frozen into a great cascade of blue-white ice, all pillars and curtains and spikes. Behind the ice the water still runs, a faint, secret sound like whispering. There is no way onward, and the only path leads back west through the thinning trees. Frozen spray has glazed every rock and twig nearby, so that the whole place glitters.
rooms.12422: The path turns north among dark spruces, whose branches droop under such loads of snow that they almost touch the ground. East, it leads back to the junction by the icy boulder. Heaps of snow that have slid from the branches lie in mounds beside the path. The forest is so silent here that the creak of your own boots seems loud.
rooms.12423: The path passes through a stand of larches, bare of needles for the winter, their thin branches etched black against the pale sky. South, it returns among the spruces; west, it continues through the forest. The snow beneath the larches is bright, catching all the light that the pines deny. The narrow slots of deer tracks cross the path in a hurried line.
rooms.12424: The path turns north at the edge of a frozen pond, a round sheet of ice dusted with snow and ringed with brittle reeds. East, the way runs back through the larches. Now and then the ice groans and cracks with the cold, a deep sound that seems to come from everywhere at once. Pines stand around the pond like a ring of silent watchers.
rooms.12425: The path runs along a narrow neck of ground between the frozen pond and a steep bank studded with stones and roots. North, it leaves the pond behind; south, it returns to the edge of the ice. Dead reeds poke up through the snow, rattling in the wind. Under the ice, where the snow has blown clear, the dark shapes of sunken logs can be glimpsed.
rooms.12426: The path turns west here, climbing away from the pond onto higher ground among old pines. South, it returns along the shore. An old hunter's lean-to of poles and bark slumps against a pine trunk, half buried in snow and long abandoned, its roof fallen in. The forest grows darker ahead, and the pines taller.
rooms.12427: The path follows a broad ridge through dark pines, east toward the old lean-to and west into deeper forest. Wind roars in the treetops, though little of it reaches the ground, and snow shaken from the branches drifts down like fine flour. The trunks are plastered with ice on one side where wind-driven snow has frozen against them. Everything around you creaks and sighs.
rooms.12428: The path dips into a shallow ravine, crossing a frozen stream bed on stepping stones capped with ice. East and west, the way climbs out of the ravine among the pines. Icicles hang from the walls of the ravine in long ranks like organ pipes, and water can be heard trickling somewhere beneath the ice. The cold in the shadow of the ravine is sharp enough to sting the eyes.
rooms.12429: Out of the ravine the path turns north, winding through a stand of pines toward a rise. East, it returns to the ravine and its frozen stream. Old stumps, felled by axes long ago, stand in the snow like grave markers, each topped with a round white cushion. Someone once logged these woods, though no one now remembers who, or where the timber went.
rooms.12430: The path crosses the top of a rise among scattered pines that let in the pale light. South, it returns among the old stumps; west, it runs along the crest. From here you can see between the trunks across a wide stretch of snowy forest, black and white to the edge of sight. The wind is keener on the rise, and it finds every gap in your clothing.
rooms.12431: The path runs along the crest of the rise between pines bent all one way by the wind. East and west the way continues along the crest. A snow-covered cairn of rounded stones stands beside the path, built by some long-gone traveller to mark the way. The wind has carved the snow around it into rippled waves and sharp little cornices.
rooms.12432: The path drops gently into a thicket of young firs, grown so close together that their branches interweave above the path. East and west, the way pushes on through the thicket, and you must stoop beneath the lowest boughs. Snow sifts down through the branches in a fine, glittering dust. The air is still and close, and smells of resin.
rooms.12433: The path comes out of the fir thicket and turns south beside a great boulder split clean in two by frost, with a young pine growing in the crack. East, the way returns through the thicket. Ahead, a steep slope of rock rises above the trees, crusted with ice and streaked with frozen meltwater. The snow here is churned by the tracks of many beasts.
rooms.12434: The path runs along the foot of the steep, rocky slope, where a narrow mountain path leads up along a ledge onto the mountainside. North, the way returns toward the split boulder; west, the main path continues through the forest. Boulders lie half buried in drifts at the foot of the slope. Pines cling to the rock above, their roots gripping it like claws.
rooms.12435: The path threads through a stretch of windthrown pines, trees flattened by some great storm and lying in a crisscross tangle. East, it returns to the foot of the rocky slope; west, it winds on between the fallen trunks. Upturned roots stand like walls, hung with icicles and frozen earth. Snow fills every gap between the trunks, hiding holes deep enough to break a leg.
rooms.12436: Beyond the windthrow the path turns south into an older part of the forest. East, it returns through the tangle of fallen trunks. The pines here are tall and straight, and around each trunk the snow has sunk into a deep, hidden well. A careless traveller who stepped off the path could plunge into one up to the chest and never climb out.
rooms.12437: The path runs on through the old forest, its snow packed hard by the passage of feet and hooves. North, it returns to the edge of the windthrow; west, it goes on beneath the pines. Lichen hangs from the branches in long grey beards that stir in the faintest breath of air. The silence is so deep that you can hear the snow settle.
rooms.12438: The path runs east and west beneath pines whose trunks are scarred with long claw marks, gouged deep into the bark far above the height of a man's head. Some of the marks are old and grey; others are fresh and still weep resin. The snow beneath the trees is churned and trampled. Something large marks its ground here, and it does not care who knows it.
rooms.12439: The path turns south at the edge of a small clearing, where the snow lies smooth and blue under an open sky. East, the way returns beneath the clawed pines. When night falls the stars blaze fiercely over the clearing, and the snow glitters back at them with its own cold light. A ring of black pines stands around the edge like a fence.
rooms.12440: The path runs west from the clearing through a stretch of forest where many of the trees are dead, their bark peeled away and their branches bare. North, the way returns to the clearing. The dead trees stand silver-grey and gaunt among the living pines, riddled with the holes of woodpeckers. When the wind blows they knock together like bones.
rooms.12441: The path turns south here and begins a long, gentle descent through the forest. East, it returns among the dead trees. The ground falls away ahead and the pines begin to thin, their trunks more and more bent by the wind. Through gaps between them, a wide white country shows beyond the edge of the wood, empty and glaring under the pale sky.
rooms.12442: The path slopes gently southward among pines that grow farther and farther apart. North, it climbs back toward the dead trees. The snow on this slope lies deep, drifted by the wind into long ridges with knife-sharp crests. A frozen creek runs beside the path, its course marked by a line of snow-buried willows whose red twigs are the only colour for miles.
rooms.12443: The path follows the frozen creek south through a little gully it has carved over the years. North, the way climbs the slope again toward the dead trees. The ice of the creek is clear as glass in places, showing pebbles and strings of trapped silver bubbles beneath. Snow-laden junipers crowd the banks, their berries a dusty blue.
rooms.12444: Here the creek bends away into a tangle of willow scrub, and the path leaves it, turning west across rolling ground among scattered pines. North, the way follows the creek back into its gully. A wooden sledge, broken-backed and half buried in snow, lies abandoned beside the path, its runners grey with age. The snow is hard-crusted here and squeaks underfoot.
rooms.12445: The path runs south through the thinning forest, where the pines stand apart and lean away from the wind. East, it returns toward the creek and the broken sledge. Snow drives between the trunks in stinging gusts, and drifts have piled against the windward side of every tree. The edge of the forest cannot be far off now.
rooms.12446: The path runs south between the last of the great pines, battered and bent by the wind that sweeps in from the open land. North, it returns into the shelter of the forest. Ahead, beyond the trees, the land opens into a white emptiness under a vast pale sky. Snow lies drifted high against the trunks, carved into smooth, curving shapes.
rooms.12447: Here the Winterwood ends, its last pines standing bent and broken at the edge of an open waste of snow. South, the way into the Winterlands is closed by a great barrier of storm-felled pines and drifted snow, piled higher than a man's head and frozen solid. North, the path leads back into the forest. The wind howls across the open land beyond, carrying a stinging haze of snow.
rooms.12456: A narrow path climbs along a ledge of rock above the forest, with a sheer drop on one side and a wall of icy stone on the other. Down below, the path returns to the forest floor; south, it leads onto a high shelf where a large cluster of great trees grows. Ice glazes the ledge, and the footing is perilous. From here the tops of the pines spread out beneath you like a dark, snow-dusted sea.
rooms.12457: The path enters a great cluster of ancient pines growing on a high shelf of the mountainside. North, it returns to the narrow, icy ledge; east, it winds on among the trees. These pines are huge and gnarled, their trunks twisted as though wrung by giant hands. The snow among them lies deep and soft, and swallows every sound.
rooms.12458: The path winds east and west among the great pines of the cluster. A massive pine has fallen across the way, and a passage has been sawn through its trunk, the cut faces dark with age and ringed with hundreds of years of growth. The air smells strongly of resin. Snow has piled along the top of the fallen giant like the crest of a frozen wave.
rooms.12459: Three ways meet among the giant pines. East, the path continues through the cluster; south, the trees open onto a snowy glade; west, the way leads back past the sawn trunk. At the junction stands the hugest pine of all, with a hollow at its base large enough for a man to shelter in. Snow lies in deep drifts between its roots.
rooms.12465: The pines here are so large that the path must wind between their roots, which hump up through the snow like the backs of buried beasts. East, the way runs on toward a rocky outcrop; south, it goes deeper among the trees; west, it returns to the hollow pine. Snow-capped boulders lie scattered among the trunks. The light is dim and grey, and very still.
rooms.12466: The cluster of pines ends against a rocky outcrop, where a way climbs up the rocks to a lookout above the trees. West, the path leads back among the giant pines. The rocks are crusted with ice and drifted snow, and the wind is stronger here. Footholds have been worn into the stone by those who have gone up before you.
rooms.12467: You stand atop a rocky outcrop high above the forest, and the whole Winterwood lies spread out below, a vast sea of black pines dusted with white. Beyond the forest a glacier glitters in the pale light, and far off snowy peaks fade into grey haze. By night the stars burn here with a fierce, cold brightness, so close it seems you could pluck them. A way leads back down the rocks to the trees.
rooms.12464: The path leads south toward the mouth of a short cave in a rocky bank, while the way north returns among the giant pines and the way west opens into a snowy glade. Large clawed tracks lead to and from the cave, sunk deep in the snow. The nearby trees are scarred and broken, their lower branches snapped off. A sour, musky smell drifts on the air.
rooms.12471: This short cave runs only a little way into the rock before ending in a rough wall. Its floor is a mess of trampled filth and scraped stone, darkened here and there with old frozen blood. The air reeks of a beast's den, thick and sour, and the walls are scored with claw marks. North, the cave mouth opens onto the snowy forest, a pale square of light.
rooms.12463: Here the giant pines draw back around a snowy glade, open to the sky. North, a path leads back to the hollow pine; east, the way goes on among the trees. Hoofprints wander across the smooth snow, pausing here and there where something has pawed down to the grass. Withered stems poke through the drifts, and in summer this must be a meadow.
rooms.12460: The narrow path squeezes through a cleft in the ridge, roofed over by a great fallen slab and a cornice of hard snow, so that you walk in a dim, close tunnel of rock. At its lower mouth the path leads back down to the forest below. South, the cleft opens into a small cluster of trees. The walls are rimed with frost, and every breath and footstep echoes back at you.
rooms.12461: A small cluster of firs grows here so densely that their snow-laden branches meet in a roof overhead, shutting out all but a dim green light. North, a path leads back into the rocky cleft; west, the trees close in around a hidden hollow. The air beneath the boughs is still and almost warm after the bite of the wind. The ground is a soft carpet of needles, barely dusted with snow.
rooms.12462: The firs close in here around a tight, hidden hollow, walled by crowding trunks and roofed by boughs bent low under their burden of snow. A gap between the trunks leads back east to the rest of the cluster. A rough platform of lashed poles has been built among the low branches, an old hunter's cache, empty now and furred with frost. The silence is so complete that you can hear your own heart.
rooms.12448: The fainter track leaves the clearing with the waymark post and turns south among the pines, narrow and little used. East, it returns to the clearing. The way winds between boulders and the trunks of old trees, and snow lies drifted against the rocks in smooth banks. Somewhere ahead, the land rises toward a dark outcrop of rock.
rooms.12449: The track runs north and south between scattered boulders, each wearing a tall white cap of snow. Pines grow among them, their roots wrapped tight around the stones. A trickle of meltwater has frozen into a glassy ribbon across the path, slick as oil. The forest is very quiet here, and the light is grey.
rooms.12450: The track ends at the foot of a rocky outcrop, where a small cave opens to the west, dark and low. North, the way returns among the boulders. The snow before the cave mouth is trampled and stained, and a rank smell, like old meat, drifts out of the dark. Icicles hang from the lip of the outcrop like a row of teeth.
rooms.12451: This small cave is low and dark, its ceiling so close that a tall man must stoop. The floor is strewn with matted fur and scraped stone, and the walls are scored with deep claw marks. The air is stale and heavy with the reek of a den, and colder even than the snow outside. East, the cave mouth opens onto the snowy forest, a dim grey shape against the dark.

16107.description: The basket is a cage of iron bars as thick as a thumb, rusted nearly through and still holding a black crust of ancient charcoal. Letters cut into the plinth have been worn by wind and rain until only one word can still be read: WATCH.

16123.description: The signs are spirals and jagged, branching lines, smeared on with a finger in something that dried the colour of old blood. A heavy chain has been wrapped around the beam and hammered shut, and the gate has not moved in a long time.

16134.description: Each face of the stone bears a simple carved arrow, softened by centuries of weather. Above the arrow that points toward the cliffs, someone has cut a raven with its wings spread wide, and the hollows of the carving are still dark with old soot.

16170.description: The spike is as thick as a thumb and driven deep into a crack in the rock. Whoever tied a rope here was either lowering something into the gulf or climbing up out of it, and the rotten strands no longer tell which.

16188.description: The blocks that fill the doorway are far cruder than the tower's own stone, and the mortar has been slapped on in haste and smoothed with bare hands. Whoever sealed this door did it from the outside, and did not mean it ever to be opened again.

16171.description: If you look long enough into the far haze you can make out a pale smudge that might be the walls of Garathorm, and at the very edge of sight a dull grey gleam that can only be the Sea of Storms.

16185.description: Seven small raven skulls, bleached and polished, are threaded on a cord between bunches of black feathers and knucklebones. Outcasts set such stakes where they keep watch, believing that the ravens will carry them word of anyone who passes.

16176.description: The figure has the hunched shoulders of a cloaked man, or perhaps the folded wings of a great bird. Its face has weathered away entirely, but the stone around its feet is polished smooth by the touch of many hands.

16137.description: The rune is cut deep and square in the dwarven fashion: a hammer above an open door. Dwarves carve it to mean the road home, and someone has rubbed it with soot to keep it clear.

16157.description: The slab is carved around its rim with a ring of runes, most of them chipped away. Heat breathes steadily through the crack across it, and if you press an ear to the stone you can hear, far below, a slow and heavy rumbling like the breath of a forge.

12403.description: Boulders as large as carts are locked in the ice like flies in amber, and deep within it a long dark shape may be the trunk of some tree that grew here before the glacier came. The ice has been carrying them for longer than anyone can say.

12414.description: The stag is carved in a few deep, sure strokes, its antlers spreading up the post. A real antler tine has been fixed into the top, grey and weathered, and hunters still tie strips of red cloth below it for luck.

12455.description: The frozen fall is as tall as a tower, its folds and pillars glowing deep blue where the ice is thickest. Bubbles hang trapped inside it like strings of pearls, and here and there a thin dark thread shows where water still slides behind the ice.

12447.description: The fallen pines lie crisscrossed as if flung down by a giant's hand, their branches locked together and cemented with ice. No one will pass this way into the Winterlands until a long thaw comes.

creatures.long_desc: A giant raven hunches on a ledge, watching you with one bright black eye.
creatures.description: It is as big as a hound, its feathers black with an oily purple sheen and its beak as long and heavy as a hatchet blade. It moves in short, stiff hops, head cocked, plainly weighing whether you are dead yet or merely soon to be. A few bright threads and a glint of tarnished silver are caught among the ruffled feathers at its throat.
rooms: On Top of the Crescent Cliffs

creatures.long_desc: An outcast scout crouches among the rocks, a loaded crossbow resting across one knee.
creatures.description: He is lean and weathered, wrapped in a cloak sewn from hundreds of black raven feathers that makes him hard to tell from the wet rock around him. An exile's brand puckers one cheek, and his eyes never stop moving. A belt of knives and a quiver of short, heavy bolts hang at his hips.
rooms: At The Base Of The Mountain

creatures.long_desc: A hulking mountain troll squats among the boulders, gnawing on something that cracks.
creatures.description: Grey-green hide as thick as bark covers its hunched body, crusted with lichen and dried mud so that, sitting still, it could pass for a boulder. Its arms hang to its knees and end in broad, cracked claws, and small red eyes glitter under its heavy brow. Around its waist it wears a crude belt of scarred hide, cut from some lesser troll it has eaten.

creatures.long_desc: A rock wyvern clings to the crag with hooked wings, its grey hide hard to tell from the stone.
creatures.description: It is a lean, long-necked beast the size of a horse, its leathery wings tipped with hooks for gripping cliffs and its hide the mottled grey of weathered granite. A barbed tail lashes slowly behind it, and its jaws are crowded with curved yellow fangs. It smells of cold stone and old blood.
rooms: On Top of the Crescent Cliffs

creatures.long_desc: A snow owl sits hunched on a low bough, its round golden eyes following your every move.
creatures.description: Its plumage is white as new snow, flecked with black at the wing tips, and so thick and soft that the bird looks twice its true size. It turns its head almost all the way around to watch you, then blinks once, slowly. Talons like hooked needles grip the bough beneath it.

creatures.long_desc: A white stag stands motionless among the pines, its breath smoking in the cold air.
creatures.description: Its coat is the pure white of fresh snow, and its antlers branch wide and pale as frosted twigs, with a dozen tines or more. It holds its head high and still, nostrils flaring, ready to bound away at the first wrong step. Old scars on its flanks tell of wolves it has outrun.

creatures.long_desc: A winter wolf slinks between the trees, pale as the snow and silent as a shadow.
creatures.description: It is bigger than any wolf of the lowland woods, with a thick coat of white and silver fur and eyes the pale blue of glacier ice. Frost rimes the fur about its muzzle, and when it bares its teeth its breath hangs in a cold cloud. Where there is one, the rest of the pack is seldom far away.

creatures.long_desc: A frost troll crouches in the gloom, its blue-white hide glittering with rime.
creatures.description: Taller than two men and gaunt as a dead tree, it has skin of a corpse-pale blue crusted with frost that never melts, and long arms ending in black claws. Icicles hang from its matted hair and beard. The cold rolls off it like a draught from an open door, carrying a stench of old meat.

items.room_desc: A cloak of glossy black raven feathers lies here in a rustling heap.
items.description: Hundreds of raven feathers have been sewn overlapping onto a backing of oiled wool, so that the cloak sheds rain like a bird's back and blends into wet black rock. It rustles faintly whenever it moves.

items.room_desc: A thick belt of grey-green troll hide lies coiled here.
items.description: A broad strip of troll hide, grey-green and tough as old boot leather, punched with crude holes and fastened with a bone toggle. Even cut from its owner, the hide seems slowly to knit its own scratches closed.

items.room_desc: A short, heavy crossbow of dark wood lies here.
items.description: A short, heavy crossbow of dark ash bound with iron, its stock carved with the slashed-through rune that outcasts take as their mark. The string is waxed against the damp, and the cocking lever is worn bright with use.

items.room_desc: A long, curved fang, yellow as old ivory, lies here.
items.description: A curved fang as long as a hand, ridged and yellow, with a groove down its inner edge where venom once ran. Alchemists and trophy-hunters pay well for such things.

items.room_desc: A tarnished silver brooch lies here, glinting dully.
items.description: A round silver brooch worked with a pattern of knotted lines, black with tarnish and bent at the pin. Ravens carry off anything that shines, and this has plainly spent years in a nest.

items.room_desc: A pale, many-tined antler lies here.
items.description: A great branching antler, pale as bone and smooth as polished ivory, with eleven sharp tines. Carvers and hunters prize the antlers of the white stags of the Winterwood and pay well for them.

items.room_desc: A thick cloak of silver-white wolf fur lies here.
items.description: The whole pelt of a winter wolf, silver-white and thick enough to turn a blizzard, cured stiff by the cold and tied at the throat by its own forelegs. The wolf's head forms a hood, its jaws framing the wearer's brow.

items.room_desc: A long bow of pale pinewood lies here.
items.description: A hunter's longbow of pale, close-grained pine, backed with sinew and wrapped at the grip with strips of fur. Whoever owned it last came to a bad end, but it still draws smooth and true.

items.room_desc: A heavy club of twisted pine root lies here, furred with frost.
items.description: A club torn from the root of a great pine, gnarled and heavy, its knotted head studded with stones hammered into the wood. Frost forms on it even beside a fire.
